title: The Forgotten Oath
premise: Sebastian Pemberton, youngest oath-keeper of the Valeward Guild, has spent his life in a valley where magic cannot cross its borders — and where the guild's true purpose is a secret even he doesn't fully understand. When the usurper King Aldric declares a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted, a wounded fugitive mage collapses at the valley's edge carrying proof that the guild's founding oath once bound an ancient war, not prevented one. Sebastian and his found family of misfit guildmates must smuggle the fugitive and the secret across a hostile realm to the free cities before Aldric's armies arrive. In the end, Sebastian learns the 'dying' guild was always meant to die with him as its last keeper — unless he breaks the oath, rekindles the old magic, and chooses a new family over a fading tradition.
about_author: X. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten guild records in provincial libraries before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven fantasy about the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet the Valeward Guild: seven members tending a border no one remembers why it exists, performing rituals that feel increasingly hollow. Sebastian tends the boundary stones alone at dusk, feeling both protected and imprisoned. Emotional beat: tender melancholy — belonging to something that may already be dead.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Odile's POV. News arrives of King Aldric's edict: all gifted persons to be seized or burned. The elders argue over whether the valley's wards can hide them forever; Odile knows they cannot. She conceals from Sebastian what the guild's original charter actually says. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in duty, a leader lying to protect her people.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Stones
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A bleeding stranger, the mage Yara, collapses against the boundary stones — the first magic Sebastian has ever witnessed. As she fades in and out, she whispers about 'the Oath' and 'the ninth name.' The guild votes, bitterly split, on whether to shelter her. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear of consequence.

chapters.title: What the Charter Says
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with Odile. Forced by crisis, Odile shows Sebastian the sealed charter: the guild wasn't founded to suppress magic but to guard the last vessel of it — and the valley's null-field is that vessel's prison. Sebastian realizes his whole life has been a wall around a secret. Emotional beat: betrayal and vertigo; identity shaken to the root.

chapters.title: Riders on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Aldric's witch-hunters reach the valley rim, led by the cold-eyed Captain Vess. The guild stages a desperate deception while Yara, half-healed, reveals the truth: the vessel is waking, and only a Pemberton blood-oath can either seal it or free it. Emotional beat: hunted-animal terror tempered by unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Vale
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Vess breaches the wards; the valley's null-field begins to fail, and with it, decades of buried memory flood back into the guildmates' minds — including Sebastian's erased childhood. The guild scatters, fleeing east with Yara toward the free cities. Emotional beat: grief and exhilaration entwined; home destroyed, self restored.

chapters.title: Road of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Guildmate Tomas's POV. On the road, the ragged band becomes a true found family: shared bread, argued maps, Yara teaching Sebastian the first sparks of his suppressed gift. But Vess tracks them, and Tomas secretly sends a false trail that may cost him his life. Emotional beat: warmth earned through sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Ninth Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Captured by Vess, Sebastian learns the usurper's motive: Aldric seeks the vessel to legitimize his stolen crown, and the 'ninth name' on the charter is Sebastian's own — written by his mother, the last true keeper. Vess offers him survival for betrayal. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal; the cost of loyalty made flesh.

chapters.title: The Oath Reforged
chapters.summary: Climax. Sebastian's POV. At the free cities' gates, with Aldric's army arriving, Sebastian speaks the broken oath anew — not sealing the vessel but sharing it, distributing the ancient magic among his chosen family rather than hoarding it in one bloodline. Vess turns her blade when shown the truth of her own erased memories. Emotional beat: triumphant defiance; the old order remade by choice, not inheritance.

chapters.title: A Guild of Our Own Making
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Sebastian's POV months later. The valley lies open; refugees and mages rebuild it as something new. Odile, aging, passes leadership not by blood but by vote, and Sebastian writes a fresh charter whose first line reads: 'We belong to each other.' The war is coming still — but they will face it together. Emotional beat: bittersweet hope; endings as beginnings.
